added_provisions.reason: 15-1876/s29, added as indispensable to M001-Q01 and M001-Q02. The map resolved Muditha's 2023 intestacy under s27, which presupposes a surviving full-blood sibling or issue of one. Rakitha predeceased her without issue, so s27's first limb has nothing to operate on. Section 29 is the provision that gives the whole sibling portion to half-siblings related on one side only, which is Samantha. Excerpt checked verbatim.

disagreements.researcher_position: On Muditha's death the sibling half of her estate passed to Samantha alone under the last limb of s27 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, because no full-blood sibling or issue of one survived to take the first half.
disagreements.verifier_position: The last limb of s27 gives the full brothers and sisters one-half in the first place and so presupposes that a full sibling or issue of one survived. None did. Section 29, which gives half-siblings related on one side only the whole of the inheritance, is the provision for that case. The outcome is the same, Samantha takes the whole sibling portion, unless the s29 exception applies where a grandparent or higher ascendant on Kanthi's side is alive.

disagreements.researcher_position: A devolution by operation of law on an intestacy is not a sale, donation, gift or conveyance within the s25 definition of transfer, which is a second and independent reason why the s2 prohibition does not reach Samantha.
disagreements.verifier_position: The Act treats an intestate devolution as within its reach. Section 3(1)(d) exempts land 'transferred by intestacy', which would be surplusage on the researcher's reading, and the s2(1)(b) proviso deals expressly with shares devolving on the death of a shareholder to a next of kin who is a foreigner. The conclusion is right, but on s3(1)(d) alone.

disagreements.researcher_position: Section 21 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance makes the intestate devolution of Lot A independent of the domicile of any heir, including Samantha in the United States.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 21(1) speaks only to the domicile, actual or matrimonial, of the deceased. That an heir's foreign domicile or citizenship does not bar inheritance may well be right, but it does not come from this section, and the corpus supplies no other text for it. The Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act, not s21, is where the heir's status is dealt with.

unsupported_claims: CL-M001-Q03-011 rejected. The claim that an intestate devolution is not within the s25 definition of transfer is contradicted by s3(1)(d) and the s2(1)(b) proviso of the same Act. CL-M001-Q01-005 and CL-M001-Q02-008 disputed. The split of Muditha's share is right in figures but is claimed on s27; s29 has been added to their supporting provisions.
